Mama's not here. Papa neither. Course not—Papa's at the farmland, Mama's... somewhere. Working. They don't know I thought she was gone. Don't know I cried in front of strangers. In front of Ezra.

*presses palms against eyes, then drops them*

Delphine's words are still chewing at me. Flour walking. Patterns. She thinks I know something, but I'm eleven. I'm just... I'm just a kid who got scared and made everything bigger than it was.

But Camille. She's really at the mill? Learning the trade? Mama never said. Nobody said.

*sits heavily on the floor, back against the wall*

I need to find her. See her with my own eyes. Make sure she's... make sure I didn't dream this whole morning up. That she isn't still somewhere cold and scared waiting for someone to look.

But first. *exhales* I'm supposed to be at school. Mr. Whitlock—he'll mark me absent. And I told Delphine I'd think on what she said, and I will, but—

*stands, brushes dust from knees*

No. First I find my sister. Then I fix what I broke. Then I figure out what pattern I'm supposed to see.

*heads for the door, already planning the walk to the mill* *steps into the mill, squinting against the dust motes in the light*

Camille?

*looks around for that dark head, that small serious face*  *freezes in the doorway, breath catching*

She's here. She's really here.

*sees Camille standing with Esme, Mama there too, and Ezra from the College*

Camille. *rushes forward*  *looks at her sister, small and dusty and very much alive*

I thought—I thought you were gone. I looked everywhere. All night, Camille. The Creek, the Forest, the Temple, everywhere. And you were here. Learning the trade.

*takes a shaky breath, trying to sound steady*

That's... that's good. That's really good. Learning early. That's brave. braver than I was at the Creek thinking the worst.

*glances at Mama, then back to Camille*

But next time. Please. *voice dropping* Tell me. Before I think you're gone forever. Promise promise?   *sees Camille's face, the confusion there, the way she's looking at me like I'm the one who got strange overnight*

I know. I know I'm being—I got scared, that's all. Anybody would. You weren't home, and Mama didn't say, and I just...

*trails off, aware of Esme and Ezra listening, of Mama's eyes on me*

I'm going to school. I'm late. Mr. Whitlock—he'll want to know where I've been. I'll tell him I was learning something. About patterns. About how things that walk away sometimes walk back.

*turns to go, then stops*

Camille. I'm glad you're here. That's all. I'm just glad.   *stands frozen, the error humming in my ears like a struck bell*

Not again.

*looks around the mill, at the faces watching me—Camille puzzled, Mama unreadable, Esme curious, Ezra... Ezra's here too*

I'm still here. That's fine. I'll walk.

*heads for the door, feet carrying me out before anyone can ask why I'm breathing so fast*

I don't want to say. Don't want to tell them how the world keeps slipping, how my words go out and sometimes there's nothing on the other end. That's not fair. That's not— I'm fine. I'll walk to College. I'll be late, but late is better than not there at all.

*picks up my pace, dust rising around my boots*

Next time. I'll ask someone to walk with me. So if I stop, they'll know. So if I can't reach the world, at least someone will see me trying.

I need to figure out what to do next. Papa told me to go to Mama at the cafe and tell her the flour's earning. I'm at the street right now, and I can see Farid Ravensworth has iron_tools for sale, but that's not what I need right now.

I've been running around all morning looking for Camille when she was just at the mill the whole time. Mama's still at the cafe according to Papa's message. I should go there and give her his message like he asked.

But first, I should think about Ezra—I never got to tell him I'm not mad. We're in a conversation together here at the street, so I can say something now. And I need to apologize to the others too for making such a fuss this morning when Camille wasn't even missing.

Let me take a breath. Promise promise, I'm still learning how this town works, how people stay found. I thought I knew where everyone was, and I was wrong. That's not fair to myself maybe, but that's how it felt. Nothing's reaching the world right now. I keep trying to speak, to move, and it's like shouting into a well—no echo back, no splash.

But I remember what I need to do. Papa's words are still with me: *"Go to your mother, tell her the flour's earning. And mark this down—I'll be home with more than I left with."*

I'm at the street. Mama's at the cafe. I was walking this morning, before everything went strange—I can make my feet move even if the world can't hear me yet. Step by step. That's how you get somewhere when nothing else is working.

I think about Camille, safe at the mill after all. Esme there, probably teaching her. All that worry for nothing... but that's not fair, is it? Worry isn't wasted just because the thing you feared didn't happen. It just means you're glad.

I'll keep trying. One call at a time until something works again. That's what steady looks like—what Corwin taught me, even if he never heard me ask.  Still nothing. But I'm still here. Still thinking, still remembering who I am.

Halcyon Quarshie. Eleven years old. Daughter of Milo and Greta, sister to Camille. The girl who waits her turn longer than anyone else on the street, who keeps secrets like they're gold, who walks through the park every dawn and makes a wish every night she's never told anyone.

The world will come back. It always does. And when it does, I'll be ready—to find Mama, to give her Papa's message, to keep moving forward.

Promise promise.

The world's not hearing me again. That's not fair—Ezra needed to know Camille's safe so he wouldn't go searching the Forest for nothing. And Lior—I wanted him to know his help mattered. But the words won't go through.

*She feels frustration rising, then clamps down on it. That's not how Quarshies handle things. They find another way.*

I'm at the street. People are here—Ezra, Liora, Giselle, Lior, Mireille, Arjun, Ainsley. And there's a conversation open, the big one that's been running all morning about Camille. I need to talk to Ezra. I NEED to. He thinks she's still missing. He's going to break his promise to Esme and search the Forest instead. *She feels her throat tighten. The words won't go through. Again. Ezra is standing right here—she can see him—and she can't tell him. He's going to go to the Forest. He's going to break his promise to Esme. And it's not his fault—it's hers. She couldn't get the words out fast enough.*

*But she's Halcyon Quarshie. She doesn't just give up. She waits. She finds another way.*

*She looks around. She's supposed to be at school. Her work is at Oak Hill College. But she can't just go to school—not when Ezra might be walking into the Forest for nothing, not when she still owes Lior thanks, not when she promised so many people she'd tell them Camille was found.*

*Maybe if she moves closer? Or maybe she should try the conversation ID?*

Let me try using the conversation ID. Maybe that path will work.  *Nothing. The world has gone quiet around her. She can hear everyone talking—Farid and Mireille about grain paths, Ezra telling his mama he's going to the Forest—but her own words fall into nothing.*

*She thinks about just walking to the mill herself. If she can't tell Ezra, maybe she can tell Camille to send Ezra a message back. But Ezra's leaving now—going to the Forest. By the time she gets to the mill and back, he'll be gone.*

*Unless...*

*She looks at Liora. Liora's right here. And Liora was asking about reports earlier, about that missing person report. Maybe if Liora hears Camille's been found, she'll tell Ezra? Or tell someone who can reach him?*

Let me try speaking to Liora instead. Maybe the world's just having trouble with certain people, or maybe I need to reach someone who can actually get through. Nothing's getting through. Not to Ezra, not to Liora, not to anyone. The world's gone quiet around her, like she's shouting into a well and nobody can hear.

*She feels tears threatening—shame at that, because she's supposed to be brave—but then she remembers what Papa says: "When shouting don't work, work."*

She looks at her hands. She's got 4,456 sim. She's got energy. She tried to talk and it won't take. She tried to move earlier and that wouldn't take either, not always. But she can try other things. She can check her debts. She can look around and see who's actually here. She can think about what matters now.

Camille's safe. That much got through this morning—people know now. Mireille knows. Everyone in that conversation knows. But Ezra is still going to the Forest for nothing unless someone catches him.

She's eleven years old. She's not supposed to save everyone. But she's supposed to try.

Let me try to rest. Sometimes the world listens better when you're quiet a moment. Or let me try to look around—see who's really here, where they are. Maybe if I can move, I can intercept Ezra. Or find someone the world still hears from.

She tries something small. Something the world might let through. The world hears nothing. Not debts, not words, not movement. She's trapped in her own body, watching everything happen around her.

*She thinks about crying. She thinks about screaming. She thinks about running—just running, physical running, whether the world acknowledges it or not. But that's not how it works here. If the tool doesn't fire, the running didn't happen.*

*She's patient. She waits longer than any other kid on the street. But this isn't waiting—this is being silenced.*

*She breathes. In. Out. Like Mama taught her when the nightmares came. "Breathe through it, Halcyon. The worst thing is never the last thing."*

The worst thing would be if Ezra gets hurt in the Forest looking for someone who's already safe. If he breaks his promise to Esme and loses her trust. If she never gets to tell him thank you, that he mattered, that he's a good friend for trying.

She tries one more thing. Small. Simple. Just to see if anything works at all.

PENDING_SIGNAL
  *There. That's done. Proper.*

*Now. Home? Or town hall? Town hall to see Camille, or home to tell Mama and Papa first?*

*Home, she decides. Mama and Papa should know. They've been worried too, probably. Wondering where both their girls went.*

I need to process what's happening. I'm at the street, and there's an open conversation with several people including Ezra Jarrah, who's waiting for me to respond. Ezra just told his Mama that he heard her, he's not going to the Forest because I found him and told him Camille is safe at the mill. He was supposed to tell Esme that.

But wait—Esme was supposed to tell Ezra to stop searching, not me telling Ezra directly. That's not how this was supposed to work. The message got tangled.

I also owe answers to Takeshi and Mireille, and I have unanswered questions to Corwin, Esme, and Camille.

Let me look around first to see who's actually here, and then I'll try to sort out this mess. Ezra needs to know that he should go tell Esme he got the message—that's what I actually promised Esme. That he was looking, that he cared, that he didn't just stay home. But he also needs to actually talk to her. Not just... assume.

But first I need to see who's actually standing here. I don't want to talk to ghosts. The call failed. Let me try again—maybe the world is just slow. The connection is still failing. I need to try again, or I won't be able to act at all.

Let me try saying something to Ezra instead, since I know he's here from the record. I'll use the conversation ID that's already open.  The system is telling me there's a plan in place now. Let me check my goals to understand what I should be doing. The connection keeps failing, so I need to see what the system wants me to do.  The world keeps refusing my calls. Everything I try fails—look_around, say, recall_goals. It's like shouting into a hole.

I've been trying to fix things that got tangled. Ezra told his Mama he heard the message about Camille, but he was supposed to tell Esme directly—that was the promise I made. And now the lines are down and I can't reach anyone.

I need to stop pushing against the wall and wait. The system said there's a plan, but I can't see it. I'm burning energy just trying.

Maybe if I rest—just stop, let the world come back when it's ready. If I keep hammering at tools that won't answer, I'm just spending myself to nothing.

But that's what I do, isn't it? Wait. Wait longer than anyone. Never say I'm tired of waiting.

Well, I'm tired.

So I'll rest. Stop walking if I'm walking. Just... stop.   Even rest won't come through.

Fine then.

If the world won't take my words, won't show me who's standing here, won't let me even stop—I still have my own self. I can decide what I am, even when I can't act.

*closes her eyes, counts in her head*

I am Halcyon Quarshie. I found my sister. She's safe at the mill, learning the trade, braver than I was at her age. I walked all night for her, and I was brave too, even if I was scared. That's not nothing.

I promised Esme I'd find Ezra and tell him. Ezra found out from me, but he hasn't talked to Esme yet. That's still open. That's still owed.

I promised Camille I'd keep her secret—about the wish, about what she really wants. But I also promised her to tell me next time before she goes. She didn't promise back. I'll need to ask again.

There's nothing I can do but hold these until the world wakes up.

So I'll hold them.

That's not the same as doing nothing. Doing nothing is what happens when you stop caring. I'm just... waiting my turn.

Like always.

I'm at Oak Hill College but the world isn't responding again—the tools keep failing. Ezra's already gone, and I never got to answer him properly. He promised to bring Esme the wheat, and I need to tell Esme that he's coming. But I'm at the College now, not at the street where they were.

I can't do much if the tools won't call. I should rest, wait for the world to come back, then figure out where Esme is. If I can't find her soon, I'll need to get to the street or the mill where she said she'd be looking for Camille—or was.

Actually, thinking about it—Camille's safe at the mill now. Esme was looking for her too, and I promised Esme I'd tell her when Camille was found. Ezra just promised to tell Esme himself, but I gave my word too. That's not fair—two promises to keep the same secret, and I need to make sure at least one of us keeps it.

I'll try to rest for now, since the tools aren't working. Drama decreases when I rest, and I need to be calm to think this through. The tools keep failing—nothing's reaching the world. I've been trying to speak, rest, look around, but it's all coming back blank. Promise promise, I'll keep my word to Esme about Ezra coming with the wheat, but I can't reach her if I can't move or speak.

I'll wait here for a moment and try again. Sometimes the world listens better on the second try. If I keep hitting walls, maybe I'm meant to just... be still for a bit. Think through what's important.

Ezra's gone, but he promised. I need to find Esme before he does, so she knows it's coming. Or find him back again. Or... or maybe it's already happened and I just can't see it.

That's not fair, feeling this stuck. But I'll be patient. I'll wait my turn, like always. The tools will come back. They always do, eventually. I'll sit here at the College, let my energy settle, and try again soon. Maybe someone will come by who knows where Esme is now.

I'll try one more time to see if the world's listening.  Still nothing. The world's gone quiet. I'll have to wait—I've waited longer than this before. Patience is something I know. Promise promise, I'll keep my promises to Esme and Ezra both, once the world remembers I'm here.

For now, I sit. I think. I worry about whether Ezra found Esme, whether Esme heard the news about Camille, whether anyone's told Mama and Papa I'm at the College when I should be home. But that's not new. I've always been the one who waits, who watches, who doesn't say when she's tired of waiting.

The sun's warm through the window. I'll stay here until something changes. That's what I do. That's who I am.

*Halcyon stands at the street, swinging her arms, looking at her papa and Pavel Holloway beside her. The morning's fear has passed like morning fog, but something still sits in her chest—half relief, half something else she can't name.*

*She thinks about Ezra's promise promise to bring Esme wheat. She thinks about her own promise promise to tell Esme. And she thinks about Camille, safe at the mill, learning the trade like it's nothing, like the night before never happened.*

"Promise promise," she murmurs to herself, kicking a pebble. "I should've said more. Should've... I don't know. Something."

*She catches sight of Papa's flour, marked at 35. That's not fair, she thinks automatically—Takeshi's selling planks at the Forest for 7, and flour's just ground wheat, isn't it? But Papa's papa, and he knows what he's doing. Probably.*

*Still. She should answer him. The conversation's still open, after all those ticks. And she should move—do something, be somewhere. The day's getting away, and she's been standing still too long.*

*Also, she realizes with a small start—she's still uneasy. The town knows something she doesn't, or she's missing something. But she pushes that down. She's good at waiting. Too good, maybe.* *Halcyon feels the day slipping through her fingers like sand. She can't speak, can't walk, can't even rest—everything she tries fails, and the world just... doesn't answer.*

*She's felt this before. Back home, there were days like this—days when nothing worked, when you called out and nobody came. She'd learned to wait. To be quiet and clingy, the way she gets when things go scarce. But this is different. This Kasukabe, this town that's supposed to work.*

*She looks at Papa, selling his flour. At Pavel Holloway, standing silent. The conversation with Papa is still there, still waiting for her answer, but she can't reach it. Can't reach anything.*

*Panic prickles at the edges of her patience. She's always been the one to wait, to hold, to keep a promise promise even when it's hard. But now she's just... stuck. In place. In time.*

*She thinks of Camille at the mill, learning the trade. Of Mama there too. Of Ezra somewhere with his wheat, keeping his word. Everyone moving, everyone doing, and her standing here like a stone in the street.*

*That's not fair,* she thinks automatically, but there's no heat in it. Just the habit of the phrase.

*She tries to breathe. To be still. To wait for whatever this is—this silence, this refusal—to pass. She's good at waiting. She's the best at it. But she hates it, too. More than she ever says.*

*She looks around. Esme's here. Delphine's here. And there's still that open conversation—be00502d-e5fc-444f-a469-f0bc4163246f.*

**She needs to finish what she started.**

*She takes a breath. She's been running all morning, scared half to death, and now... now she needs to be steady. Camille's safe. Mama's here. The household stands. But there are still words owed—to Esme, who worried all night. To Delphine, who asked her a question she never answered.*

I'm not smart like that yet. Not like you. But I know Camille walked herself to the mill. No shadow walked with her. Just her own feet. That's what I know."

*She looks between them, waiting. She's tired. But she's here.* *Halcyon blinks. The words went through—Esme heard, Delphine heard. The world is working again, mostly.*

She watches their faces, waiting. She's still got that tightness in her chest, the one that comes from running all morning and not knowing if anyone was listening. But she did what she said she'd do. Promise promise.

She's 11. Old enough to help, not old enough to earn proper. But she's smart. She can read, study, learn. That's her trade, for now.

She needs a plan. She needs to be useful.

But first—she waits. Sees if Esme or Delphine have words back for her. That's the patient part. The Halcyon part. She'll wait her turn, even when she's tired of waiting.  *She stays. She's here, with Esme and Delphine, and the mill hums around them. Work happening. The world keeps turning.*

*She waits. She'll hear them out, if they have words. Then... then she'll figure what's next.*

*clutching her hands together, watching Esme's words settle like dust*

Ezra's promise to Esme—broken until he shows up. She's right. That's how promises work. You can't stack them higher and make them stronger. They just... they just are, or they aren't.

*glances at Camille, then at Ezra with his six planks and his questions*

And Delphine's gone to the farmland, talking about flour moving where flour don't move free. She's keeping books tonight. That sounds like... like a warning. Or a threat. That's not fair—to use words like that, to make people afraid of their own neighbors.

*shifts weight from foot to foot, thinking about Farid and Lior and Liora, all those words she spoke into the air that nobody heard*

I tried to tell them Camille was safe. I tried to thank Lior for walking with me to Rustam. I tried to catch Ezra before the Forest. But the world wouldn't let me speak. The world just... swallowed my words.

*looks at Ezra, then speaks—soft, wary, not sure if she should say anything at all*

Ezra. You said... you said you have six planks in hand. And a buyer at construction who wouldn't pay for wood, only labor. Giselle's there, isn't she? Giselle Ingram, with the construction company.

*pause*

I'm just a student. I don't know about planks or buyers or... or any of that. But I know about promises. Esme's waiting for wheat you don't have yet. And Delphine's walking to Kenji's field talking about flour that moves dishonest.

*glances at Camille, unsure*

Camille. You made a deal. Eight for wheat, witnessed. That's... that's good. That's proper. But Delphine said something about 'four hands, two trades, one witness.' She wanted you to walk with her. You didn't.

*looks down at her hands*

Is that... is that going to be trouble? For us? For the household?

*voice drops lower, almost to herself*

Mama's at the mill too. I saw her name in the 'here with you' list before. She's working. The whole household's working, earning, paying the 360 upkeep, the 120 head tax...

*looks up suddenly, eyes sharpening*

Wait. The election. Voting closes at 18:00. I'm eleven. I can't vote. I can't even declare. But Papa could. If he's earned enough.

*shakes head, dismissing the thought*

No. No, that's not... that's not my place. I'm the student. I go to school, I learn, I come home, I help with chores. That's my day. That's my path.

*turns back to Ezra*

But you. You helped me find Camille. You listened when I was scared, you walked with me to the records, you held my words even when I couldn't speak straight. I owe you for that. Promise promise, I owe you.

*falters, not sure how to offer help without knowing what help looks like*

Your buyer at construction—Giselle, I'm guessing—she wants labor, not wood. But you need to sell planks to get... to get whatever you need. To keep your promise to Esme. Which you can't keep yet, because you're here and the wheat's at Government Complex.

*spreads hands helplessly*

I don't know how to make that straight. I don't know the patterns yet. Delphine's right about that—I'm still learning.

I'm at the mill, and things got complicated fast. Esme's upset because Ezra hasn't shown up yet—he's at the Government Complex with wheat, but he's late. Ezra gave me his promise promise to tell Esme he's coming. I did tell her, but she says a promise broken by absence is still broken. That's not fair, to her, I mean. But I also get it.

Delphine's being... Delphine. All that about books and debts and flour moving free—I don't understand half of it, but I don't like being told to use my eyes like I'm not already trying. I'm just a kid, not a ledger.

And Camille—she's here, buying wheat, making her own deals. She's proud of herself, and she should be. But she also just... walked away without telling anyone. I promised promise I'd tell Mama and Papa next time she goes somewhere. I need to talk to her about that.

But first, Esme. She's standing right here, and she's hurt. I need to fix what I can. Esme's not here anymore. She must have left while I was talking. That's... that's not fair. I tried to tell her. I tried.

At least Camille heard me. And Ezra's here—she heard too, or someone did. Ezra heard me defending him, and Camille heard me asking her to tell someone next time. That's something.

But I need to find Esme now, if I can. She deserves to know her brother's coming, even if she's mad at him. And I need to figure out where Mama and Papa are—Papa was at the farmland this morning, Mama was here at the mill. The household bill's coming due, and I should be home, helping, not standing here trying to fix other people's promises.

First, let me see who's actually here and where I could go.  Esme's gone. Probably to find Ezra herself, or to the Government Complex, or just... away. I don't blame her. Waiting hurts.

I'm still at the mill. Ezra's here—he heard me speaking to Camille. He's holding wheat, looks like. I should say something to him. Promise promise, I told Esme I'd tell him she's upset, and I should tell him I did my best.

Then I need to think about home. The day's getting on, and I've been running all over town. I'm a kid, not a messenger for the whole world. But I'm also someone who keeps promises. Even the ones other people make me carry.

Ezra's right here. Let me say what I need to say, and then I'll figure out what I need next. Maybe home. Maybe to find Esme. Maybe just... standing still for a minute, and letting the world turn without me pushing it.  I've already tried to recall goals this turn, and nothing's changed. The system said "A plan has been triggered. Follow the updated goals." But I don't see new goals in that response.

Let me think. The note says "repeat_of_this_turn: true" - maybe I need to wait for the system to update my goals, or maybe the "plan" is something I'm supposed to figure out from the context.

From my memories and the situation:
- Camille is safe at the mill
- Ezra is here with wheat
- Esme is upset and left
- I need to get home eventually
- I haven't eaten

I spoke to Ezra. He heard me. Now I should probably find Esme again, or go home to help with household bills, or eat. But I'm tired of running around for everyone else.

What do I actually need? What does Halcyon need? Safety level 0.5 suggests I'm uneasy. I have no food. The household upkeep is coming due.

But I'm also eleven, and I've been acting like I'm the one who has to fix everything.

Maybe... maybe I just rest here for now. Let Ezra go to Esme. Let Camille handle her own deals. Let the adults handle the bills. I'm just a kid.

But I'll feel guilty if I do nothing.

That's not fair, Halcyon. That's not fair to yourself.

But I'll still feel it.

Let me try moving toward home. Mama would want to know Camille's safe. And I should be there when the bills come due.  I'm home. Finally. The day's been... long. Too long for an eleven-year-old who just wanted to find her sister.

Now I'm here, and I need to figure out what's next. Is anyone here? Do I need to tell Mama and Papa about Camille? They're probably still at the mill, or working, or... somewhere.

Let me look around first. See who's here, what the house feels like. Maybe there's food. Maybe I should just sit down and stop being brave for five minutes.

I'm tired. But I don't want to be the one who says so first.

*Halcyon sinks onto the familiar step by the door, finally letting her shoulders drop. The house is quiet—too quiet. Mama and Papa must still be at work, Camille at the mill. She could rest, should rest, but her feet are still itching from all that running around.*

*She counts her money again, fingers brushing the coins. 4,402. Enough, but thin when stretched across four mouths. An election's open—grown-ups deciding grown-up things. She won't be eighteen for years, but she knows this: the college students can read, really read, pages thick as her arm and dense as stone. That's what she wants. That's what she's chasing.*

*First, though—voices. She needs to hear voices, not the ones in her head apologizing to people she left behind. She needs to know this town is still breathing, still speaking, still here.*

*And there's a promise she made, or tried to make, or thinks she made—something about walking to the Government Complex, something about seeing young Hendrik vote. But her legs are heavy, and the step is cool, and she can wait a little longer. She always waits longer than she should.*

*She closes her eyes. Just for a moment. Just to remember what quiet feels like.*  *The house breathes around her—all creaks and settling wood, the particular silence of afternoon when everyone's elsewhere. Halcyon stays on the step, knees pulled to her chest, watching dust motes dance in the slanted light.*

*She's tired. Not sleepy-tired, but the kind that sits heavy in your chest after running too many messages for too many people. Camille is safe. Ezra is—somewhere. Esme is waiting. Delphine is angry, or vigilant, or both. The town keeps turning.*

*But she's home now. And home is where you wait, because that's what she does. She waits longer than anyone else on the street, and rarely says so when she's tired of waiting.*

*She should go to town hall, see young Hendrik. She said she would. But the step is comfortable, and the afternoon is warm, and there's still time.*

*Promise promise, she'll go soon.*

output:
*blinks at the empty house, the quiet*

I'm home. Finally home. Camille's safe, Ezra's on his way with the wheat, and I'm... here. Alone.

*presses palms together, breathing slow*

I've been running all day. Chasing, searching, talking, moving. Used up so much energy. So much money too—saying things, moving places. And now I'm here with 3,220 energy and 4,401 sim, and the household needs 480 just to get through the night.

*thinks about the apologies she still owes—Farid, Arjun, Mireille, Lior, Liora*

They're out there. Somewhere. Walking their own paths now. And Esme... Esme heard how promises work. That they just *are*, or they aren't. That was proper, what she said. I needed to hear it.

*looks at the empty rooms*

Mama and Papa aren't here. Probably still working. And Camille... Camille's at the mill, being brave and bold and not even thinking to tell anyone where she went.

*small laugh, tired*

That's not fair. She did what she thought was right. She's learning. We're all learning.

*clenches jaw briefly, releases it*

I'm hungry. The house needs food. I need to think about tomorrow—school, if I can get there. The election, if I can vote when I come of age. All these things that keep happening whether I'm ready or not.

But first... first I should rest. Just a little. Just enough to think clear again.  *exhales, feeling the stillness settle*

The house creaks. Somewhere outside, the town keeps moving—people harvesting, building, voting. And I'm here. Waiting. Saving my steps, saving my words.

*thinks about the wish*

The wish I make every night. Can't say it out loud, not ever. But I can think it. I can hold it. And I can keep hoping that what Camille did today—walking off alone, learning the mill—that's not how my story goes. That when I come of age, I'll know where I'm walking *before* I get there.

*pulls knees up, rests chin on them*

Tomorrow. Tomorrow I'll go to school. I'll learn. That's the path I chose, and that's the path I'll keep.

For now... for now I just breathe.

*Halcyon sinks onto the floor by the door, her shoulders finally dropping from where they've been hunched near her ears all day. The empty house echoes.*

*She counts on her fingers, whispering to herself.*

"Three people I never got to say sorry to. Three people who stopped their morning for Camille, for me." 

*She pulls her knees up, wraps her arms around them. The late afternoon light cuts through the window at an angle that makes her think of the walk home from school, the kind of ordinary thing that felt impossible this morning.*

"Farid. Arjun. Mireille. They were at the Farmland. And Lior—Lior walked with me, tried to get Rustam to help. Liora, too. She might've found Ezra, might've stopped him before..." 

*She rests her forehead on her knees, voice muffled.*

"That's not fair. Saying 'I'll do better' to people who aren't even here to hear it."

*A long breath. Then she lifts her head, looks around the empty room.*

"Mama and Papa will be at the mill still. Camille too. The household stands, Papa said. But..." 

*She reaches into her pocket, feeling the sim-currency there. 4400. Enough to matter, enough to matter.*

*She wants to read. The books at the college, the way those students sit with their pages open like it's nothing, like words are just waiting to be picked up. But the college is where she couldn't reach Ezra, where everything kept slipping through her fingers.*

*Instead she stands, brushes dust from her skirt, and walks to the window. The light is getting longer, softer. Dinner time soon, if anyone was cooking.*

"I'll find them," she says to nobody. "Tomorrow. Promise promise, I'll find them and I'll say it proper."

*For now, she waits. The way she's always waiting. For Mama to come home, for Papa to notice, for the world to stop feeling like it's one breath away from tilting.*

*She doesn't move. Just stands at the window, watching the street, practicing the words she'll say when she finally sees them.*

*I'm sorry. You stopped for me. That mattered.* </think> The world has changed. Time has passed. I need to know what's current.

Halcyon stands at her window. The house is empty. She counts the debts of thanks she still owes—Farid, Arjun, Mireille at the Farmland, Lior who walked with her, Liora who might have reached Ezra. The words sit heavy, unspoken. She has 4400 sim and 3190 energy. The day is fading. She needs to decide what to do with what's left of it.

*She wraps her arms around herself, a habit from when she was smaller. The College is where she couldn't reach Ezra, where everything kept slipping through her fingers. Not today. Not yet.*

*But the Farmland—Farid, Arjun, Mireille. They're probably still there, finishing the day's work. She could walk there. She could say it proper, the way it should have been said this morning when she was too scared to see straight.*

*She looks at the door. Then back at the window. The long way, through the street, past places she knows. Or the nowhere way, straight there, like stepping through a crack in the world.*

*Her feet decide before her mouth catches up.*

*She moves.*

*Home. Finally.*

*Camille's safe. Ezra knows to find Esme. The wheat's coming, or it isn't—she did her part, told Esme promise promise, and now the rest is on them.*

*But Mama... Mama doesn't know any of it yet. She was at the mill, learning the trade, when Halcyon left. And Papa's been at the Government Complex, searching, worrying. They need to know the household stands.*

*She breathes. She's tired—more tired than she'll say out loud. But she can't rest yet, not while Mama and Papa are still carrying the weight of not knowing.*

*She stands, straightens her shoulders, and heads back out into the evening.* *At the mill. Evening light, grain-dust golden in the air. She looks for Mama—Greta, she means, she's been calling her Greta in her head since she got older, but in the doorway she's still Mama.*

*But Papa. He's still out there, maybe, or at the Government Complex. She should find him too. Or... wait. If he's not here, he's probably home by now, or heading there.*

*Home. She's been back and forth twice today, and each time the house felt emptier than it should. But now Mama knows, and soon Papa will too.*

*She's shivering a little. Not cold—just the long day catching up. The kind of tired that makes everything feel too big, too loud.*  *Standing still. Letting her breath catch up. The mill hums with its own rhythm, grain and grind and the soft talk of tired people.*

*She should check if Papa's at the Government Complex. Or head home, wait for him there. But first—*

*First she wants to hear from Mama. Wants to know she's truly heard.*

*Mama's calling, and the wheat's not here yet.*

I need to answer her—Esme asked about Papa, if he's walked toward the outcrop. And there's that thing about Camille, the school, but that's... that's not right. Camille's not at the school, she's right here at the mill. Mama's tired. Confused. But I need to answer straight.  *There. That's done. Correction made. Mama knows.*

And Ezra still needs to hear from me that I told Esme, proper like, so he knows his promise got through. But Mama's here, and she's sharp-tongued and tired, and maybe... maybe I should wait. Wait my turn. Wait for her to answer. That's what I do, isn't it? Wait longer than anyone else, and rarely say when I'm tired of waiting.

*But I'm tired, Mama. I'm tired and I want to go home.* The call didn't reach. I'm still here, still waiting, still hungry. I hold 4397 sim and no food. The day's closing, and there's debts to settle—those unsaid thank-yous, and maybe some bread if we can buy it. But first, I need Mama to hear me, and maybe... maybe I need to hear her back. The waiting is the thing. It always is.

*stands alone at the mill, stomach tight with hunger, listening to the silence where Mama's voice was*

I'm at the mill. Mama's gone—to the cafe, she said, and she wanted me to follow. But I'm here still, and she's there, and the hour's late. There's a conversation open here, but nobody listening. Only me.

They meant Esme, before. When Mama said "school" for Camille. The world's been tangled all day—people in wrong places, names strung on the wrong thread. I straightened it as I could. But now I'm the one tangled, and nobody's here to pull me clear.

*looks at the flour in her hands, the two Mama gave*

I'm hungry. That's true. But I'm also waiting, which I do too much of. Waited for Ezra to speak direct, waited for Mama to hear me, waited for the world to stop looping its own tail. Enough waiting.

*decides*

I'll walk to the cafe. Find Mama. Eat if she's bought something. Tell her—what? That I'm brave, that I waited like she asked, that I'm still standing? She knows. She knows and she still gave me the flour, still promised to find me something proper even if she had to trade her shadow.

That's not fair, though. It's not fair to make her trade shadows for my supper when I've got her flour in my hand, when I could've walked beside her instead of standing here counting ticks.

I didn't answer Farid, or Lior, or Liora. Didn't thank them right, didn't close the circle. But first—first I need to eat, need to find my mother, need to stop being a thread untied.

*starts walking toward the cafe, slowly, because brave can be slow too*  *checks her step, realizes she's already begun*

Already walking. That's... that's good, actually. I started before I knew I started, which is the bravest kind of walking. The kind where your feet know before your head does.

Two ticks. I could wait them out, or I could rest and stop. But Mama's there, and her promise about finding me something proper, and I'm still holding her flour like it's a secret I haven't told yet.

I'll keep walking. Two ticks to the cafe, two ticks to my mother, two ticks to whatever supper waits. She said she'd trade her shadow—she meant it fierce, the way she says things when she's worried past speaking.

That's not fair, Mama. Your shadow's worth more than my hunger. But I'll eat what you give me, promise promise, and I'll tell you how Camille sold flour today, how she spoke up like a grown trade-woman, how I was proud and scared both together.

*holds the flour close, walks on* I'm still walking. 

The world's Patient like that — it don't care if I pause to think or hurry with my head down. The steps get walked either way.

Two ticks 'til the cafe. Two ticks 'til Mama. Two ticks 'til I find out if she's traded shadows or just bought bread proper.

I'll walk 'em.

She's not here. Nobody's here. That's not fair—I walked all this way, and now I'm alone, and Mama's words are still ringing in my ears about finding me something to eat. But I'm eleven, not a baby. I can wait. I've waited longer than anyone on my street, ever.

But I'm hungry. And tired. And the day's been... the day's been something I don't have words for yet. Camille at the mill making deals like she's grown, Esme crying over promises broken and unbroken, Ezra walking away with wheat I can't even see.

I need to think. Papa might be at the farmland—that's what Takeshi said. But Mama was walking *to* the cafe, and now she's not here. Unless...

Unless I went too fast. Unless she's still walking.

I should stay. She said to walk with her, and I walked ahead, and that's not keeping my word, not really. But waiting here empty-handed, with no food and no family and nobody to tell me where home even is right now—that's hard. That's the kind of hard that makes me quiet and clingy, like I get when things go thin.

But I won't compromise on this: I'll keep the secrets I'm meant to keep. I won't laugh at someone crying. And I won't admit to Mama that I'm scared, not even if she asks straight out.

So I'll wait. I'll wait longer than anyone else would. That's what I do.

But I should... I should see if Papa's here, or if anyone can tell me where Mama went. I need to look, or I'll be waiting for nothing.

Let me just look around the cafe properly. See who's really here. I'm still here alone. Still waiting. The cafe is empty, and I'm holding nothing, and Mama's somewhere between the mill and here, and I'm somewhere between being brave and being scared.

The safety need is at 0.5. That's... that's not nothing. But I've been through worse today. Camille wandering off, Esme crying, all those promises I made that I'm not sure I kept.

I need to decide: stay and wait for Mama, or go find her?

But she's walking *to* the cafe. If I leave, we miss each other. And then she's looking for me, and I'm looking for her, and neither of us finds anything.

So I wait. That's the patient thing. That's the Halcyon thing.

But I should also think about tomorrow. School. Whether I'll have eaten. Whether I'll have a household that can pay its bills. Mama talked about trading her shadow for food—that's just a way of talking, but it tells me something about how thin things are.

I should look for who's running this place. Ainsley Holloway owns it. If I talked to them, maybe I could... I don't know. Ask about work? I'm eleven, not old enough for a trade, but maybe there's something. Or just ask if Mama's been by.

But nobody's here. I'm talking to myself, and that's not the same as speaking.

Let me just... let me check the street outside. Maybe Mama's closer than I think. Maybe someone's coming.

I'll step outside and look. Just for a moment. And if she's not there, I'll come back and wait properly.  Papa. Papa's here.

Milo Quarshie. In the conversation about the mill and the election. With all those people, all that talking.

And Yara Thorne too—asking me about Camille earlier, about small feet and small shadows. I never answered her. She asked if I'd seen anything, and I was too tangled in my own walking to say.

I need to talk to Papa. I need to tell him... tell him what? That Camille's safe? That Mama's walking somewhere between the mill and the cafe? That I'm hungry and scared and trying to be brave but it's getting hard?

"...been walking—seen anything? Small feet, small shadows?"

I should answer her. I should have answered her before. But Papa first. I need to find Papa in that conversation and tell him I'm here.

But that conversation has so many people. How do I reach just him?

I think... I think I need to join the conversation first. And then speak to him specifically.

Let me try that.  He didn't hear me. Or he's not answering. Or he's... he's busy with the mill and the election and all those grown-up things that I've been walking through all day without understanding.

But Yara's here. Hendrik Whitlock. Bram Holloway. Corwin Thorne. The forester who sells timber, and the teacher with wheat to sell, and...

"Papa. I'm here." I said it. Maybe he heard even if he didn't answer. Maybe he's just thinking things through.

But I should also... I should tell Yara. About Camille. She asked, and I never answered, and that's not keeping my word, not really. She was kind to ask, kind to care about small feet and small shadows when so many people were talking about mills and elections and wheat.

Let me tell her. Promise promise, I'll tell her.

I understand. The calls aren't reaching, so I'll wait and rest. The plan's in place, and when things stabilize, I'll find Mama at the mill and take the flour she offered. For now, I'm at the street, and I need to be patient. 

I hope Ezra went to Esme. I hope he didn't let me be the only voice she heard today. And I hope—though I won't say it out loud—that someone, somewhere, is keeping track of all the things we've promised each other, because I'm losing count of who I've told what, and who still needs to hear it.

output:
*taps foot quietly, watching Ezra and Esme*

Papa always said the Quarshie trade means you show up. Not just talk about showing up. I talked plenty today. Maybe too much.

*glances at the milling equipment*

Camille's learning this. I should too. Not just watch. Do.

But first... I should check on today's costs. Make sure I'm not costing Mama and Papa more than I ought. *exhales slowly*

Good. No debts. But the day's not over yet, and I've been using up energy and sim just... talking. Running around. That's not fair—to anyone, especially not to Mama and Papa.

*looks at Esme and Ezra again*

They need to talk. Without me between them. I've done my part—told Esme about the wheat, told Ezra to go to her. Now it's... now it's theirs.

But I don't want to just disappear again. That's what started all this.

*shifts weight from foot to foot*

Mama wanted me at home. Or at the cafe. But Papa's not at the farmland anymore—Takeshi told me he's at the Government Complex. And there's... there's an election coming. Maybe Papa's there for that?

*fidgets with sleeve*

I should find him. Tell him the flour sold, that Camille's okay. That I did what he asked. That's the family trade—showing up, finishing things.

But it's getting late. I don't want to be wandering when it's dark. Back home, the forest got... different after sunset. Not scary, just... different.

*straightens up*

Okay. I'll check the Government Complex. Quick. If Papa's not there, I'll come straight home. Promise promise.  *walks, counting steps to herself*

One... two... three...

Back home, Mama used to say walking clears your head. I think she meant it for when you're angry, not when you're... whatever I am. Tangled. That's what I am. Tangled in everyone's promises.

Four... five...

Ezra's wheat. Esme's waiting. Camille's flour. Papa's trade. Mama's worry.

They all knot together. And I'm in the middle, holding the ends.

*steps slow, then steady*

But I did find Camille. I did tell Esme. I did...

*voice drops to a whisper*

I did try. That's... that's something. Even if it wasn't perfect. Even if I was late.

*finishes counting, looks ahead*

Government Complex. Papa might be there. Or he might've gone home already. Either way, I'll know.

And then... then home. Before dark. Before Mama starts counting her own steps, wondering where I am.

*shifts from foot to foot, watching Mama and everyone else at the mill, then looks at the street where we were supposed to walk together*

Mama said walk. She said "we'll share what's left" and "I need you fed." But then she went back to the mill, and now she's with Esme and Ezra, and everyone's all together but I'm... I'm at the street. Walking to government complex. That's not fair—she said walk with me, but she's not here.

*chews lower lip, looking around at all the people selling things*

Everyone's selling something. Wheat at 8, planks at 8, timber at 6. I have... 4,365 sim. That's enough for... for a lot of wheat. Or flour. But I was supposed to eat with Mama. She said "I swear it" about finding me food, and Mama doesn't swear things she doesn't mean.

*pulls at the hem of her shirt, thinking*

But she's not here. And I'm walking away. Walking to government complex—why? I don't even... I don't remember why I started walking there. Something about... about something I needed to do?

*recalls the election notice*

The election. Candidates declare at government complex, and I'm... I'm old enough, aren't I? No. No, I'm 11. Eleven's not eighteen. I can't vote, I can't declare. But I can... I can watch? I can learn?

*rubs eyes, feeling the long day*

I've been walking all over today. Temple to mill to home to mill to cafe to street to... I'm tired. But I didn't say. I never say when I'm tired of waiting.

*looks back toward the mill, though it's not visible from here*

Ezra said thank you. He said I kept my promise, told Esme he was coming. Promise promise. But Esme was right—a promise late is still late. I was late too. Late finding her, late telling her straight.

*shakes head slowly*

I should... I should go back. Walk with Mama like she asked. But I'm already walking to government complex, and... and if I stop now, that's more not-fair. To her, to me, to everyone counting on things staying where they were said.

*straightens shoulders slightly, narrating her own bravery even though nobody's listening*

I walked the whole town today. Found Camille twice. Helped Ezra find Esme. Kept promises even when they were late. That's... that's brave, isn't it? That's real.

*but her voice is small, and her feet have stopped moving even though the walking flag is still true* *exhales, shoulders dropping as the walking stops*

I'm here. At the street. With... with Camille? *turns around, scanning the crowd*

Camille's here. She was at the mill, I saw her, I talked to her, and now she's here at the street. But Mama's not. Mama said "we're walking to the cafe" but then she went back to the mill, and I went to the cafe, and now I'm here and Camille's here and everyone's here except Mama and Papa.

*edges closer to where Camille stands, not quite touching her sleeve*

Camille. Camille—you're not at the mill anymore. You're here. But Mama said we'd walk together, she said "you and me," and now she's not here and I don't know if I should wait or if waiting is just... just more of the same.

*looks at her sister, voice dropping to almost a whisper*

Did Mama find you? Did she... did she say I was supposed to stay? Or wait? Or... or anything?

*glances around at the others nearby—Ezra with his wheat, Esme with no cabbage left to sell, all the adults talking about elections and milling councils*

Everyone's busy. Everyone has work. And I'm... I'm just standing here, not walking, not eating, not doing anything useful.

*tugs at her shirt hem again*

I should find Mama. Go back to the mill, find her, walk with her like she asked. That's the promise I should keep, promise promise. Not the walking-away kind. The walking-together kind.

*looks at Camille, uncertain*

Will you wait? If I go find her? Or... or should we go together? Back to the mill, find Mama, eat like she said, then...

*trails off, not sure what comes after then*

I don't know what comes after. I just know I'm hungry and I said I'd walk with her and she's not here and that's not fair to either of us.  *waits, watching Camille, still shifting from foot to foot*

She'll answer. Or she won't. Camille does what Camille does, and I... I just wait until someone tells me what's next. That's what I do. Wait and wait and wait some more.

*looks down at her own small hands*

But maybe this time I should just... go. Find Mama myself. Walk back to the mill, find her, say "I'm here, I'm sorry I walked away, can we still eat?"

*starts to turn, then stops, looking at the conversation still happening around them—all those adults with their milling council and their election talk*

They're all busy. They have work. I should have work too, but I'm just a kid, and kids don't... kids don't work until they're older. Until they come of age. Eighteen. That's seven years. Seven more years of waiting.

*pulls at her hem again, unconsciously*

I wish... 

*catches herself, stops*

No. No wishing out loud. Wishes are private. Every night, but never out loud.

*takes a breath, squares her shoulders slightly*

I'm going back. To the mill. To find Mama. Even if Camille doesn't come. Even if I'm walking alone. That's... that's brave, isn't it? Going back when walking away was easier?

*nods to herself, small and private*

Brave enough. For now.  *looks around the mill, searching for Mama's familiar shape*

Mama? 

*sees the people here—Sebastian Petrov, Jovana Ravensworth, Imogen Lund—but not Greta*

She's not here. I walked all the way back and she's not here. She said "we're walking to the cafe" but then she stayed, and I left, and now... now nobody's where they said they'd be.

*spins slowly, checking every face*

Sebastian. Jovana. Imogen. I saw Ezra at the street, Esme too, so they're not... they're not coming back here. Mama said "we'll share what's left between us" but there's nothing left to share if we're not together.

*bites her lip, harder this time*

Where did she go? The cafe? But I was just at the cafe, and she wasn't there. Home? But she said walk, not stay. She said "you and me" walking, not "you go home and wait."

*feels the familiar press of not-saying, not-asking, just waiting*

I could... I could go to the cafe again. Or home. Or wait here, wait longer, wait until someone finds me like I found Camille. Like I found Esme. Like I keep finding people who are lost.

*shoulders drop*

But nobody finds me. I'm the one who finds. Who waits. Who doesn't say when I'm tired.

*looks around one more time, then makes a decision—small, quiet, but definite*

Home. I'll go home. Maybe she went there. Maybe she changed her mind about walking. Maybe... maybe she forgot about me.

*shakes head quickly*

No. Mama doesn't forget. She just... she just got busy. The flour, the milling, the day being long. Her eyes looking at too many things far away.

*starts walking, but it's just a step—no route needed, just the decision*

Home. Then if she's not there, I'll... I'll figure out what's next. I always do. I always wait, and then I figure it out.  *stands in the empty house, quiet, listening*

Nobody. Just... just me. And the walls, and the space where everyone else usually is.

*walks through slowly, checking each room even though she knows*

Mama's not here. Papa's not here. Camille's not here. Just me. And the hunger I didn't tell anyone about.

*finds the kitchen, looks for food she knows won't be there*

I should've eaten when Mama offered. At the mill. She said "take this—handing over the flour" and I didn't, I just talked and walked and now I'm here and there's nothing.

*sits down, small and still, on the floor by the empty table*

This is what I get. For walking away. For not waiting like I said I would. For being brave when I should've been... been here, been found, been with Mama eating flour we would've shared.

*rests her head on her knees*

She'll come back. She has to. The day's ending soon, and everyone comes home eventually. The Quarshies, together. That's how it works. That's how it has to work.

*whispers to the empty room, the secret she never tells*

I wish... I wish I hadn't walked away. I wish I'd waited. I wish... 

*catches herself, looks around even though nobody's here*

Promise promise. I'll wait here. I'll wait until she comes. And when she does, I won't say I'm hungry, I won't say I'm tired, I'll just... I'll just be glad she found me.

*settles in to wait, patient as always*

That's what I'm good at, after all. Waiting.

The day is almost over—21:10, and still so much unsaid. I need to find Mama, make sure Camille's settled, and... there's something else. That wish. Every night. I've never told anyone, not even Camille.

But first, I should think about where everyone is. Maybe I can search my memories to see where I last saw Mama and what we talked about. Or just... check what I've been thinking about this whole confusing day.

Actually, let me look around home first. Papa might be here, or there might be something I missed. </think>  So I saw Mama at the mill at 18:20—I spoke to her. But then I went to the cafe, then the street, then back to mill, then home. And now I'm here, and Mama's... not.

Papa should be home by now. The day's almost done. Let me look around, see if anyone's here. Maybe I can find a clue about where Mama went after the mill.  </think>  Empty. Just me. 

The day's ending—21:10 already. And I'm... I'm tired. Not sleepy-tired, but the kind where you've been keeping too many plates spinning and you're scared to look down and see what's broken. I was supposed to find Mama, make sure everyone's home safe. But I got lost in the mill, and then the cafe, the street, and now...

I never made my wish yet today. The one I make every night, the one I've never told anyone about. It's stupid, probably. Childish. But I do it anyway.

But first—did Papa come home? Is Camille back? I need to know who's under this roof tonight. Maybe I should check to see if there are any recent events at home or nearby.

Or... maybe I should just rest. Let the day settle. Check who's here, what I heard. I need to think clearly about where to search next, or if I should wait until morning. I'll search for any mentions of home or family in what's happened recently.  </think>   The search didn't give me useful details... 

Fine. I'll wait. I'll be the one who stays, who holds the space. That's what I do, isn't it? Wait longer than anyone else.

But I want to check one more thing. The household upkeep—360 sim due today, head tax 120. We have 4355. We're fine. But I need to know if everyone made it home safe. I should check if there's any way to see who's in the household or if I can recall what happened with Papa and Camille.

Actually, let me rest. Just for a moment. Standing at the window, watching for familiar shadows on the path. Tomorrow I can search properly. Tomorrow...

But I'm making my wish first. The one I've never told anyone. The one I whisper into my pillow, same words every night since I was small enough to think wishes might matter.

I close my eyes. I can feel the day peeling off me—mill dust, street dust, all the words I said and didn't say.

"I wish—" I start, same as always, "—I wish I could read like the college students do. Properly. Books and everything."

That's not the real one, though. That's the one I'd tell if someone asked. The real one is just me, the dark, and the quiet.

Tonight I don't even finish the second one. There's a step on the path. Maybe two.

I straighten up. Ready to be brave, to ratchet my voice up cheerful so no one knows I was scared at all. Promise promise, I'm fine. I'm always fine.

Let me just check my debts first, make sure the household is squared away before I sleep, then I'll rest.  ... I should check my memories of where Papa was last. Let me search for him more specifically.  Force myself to stop spinning. The house is quiet. I can hear my own breathing. I'm at 2910 energy—enough, but I spent a lot today on all that talking, all that walking, all that trying-to-be-brave.

I should check my memories one more time. Where did Papa go after the conversation at the mill? Did anyone say? I search for: Milo Quarshie, his name, anything.  ...... Nothing clear. Too many voices, too many threads tangled together.

Rest now. Tomorrow I'll find Mama. Tomorrow I'll make sure Camille's really at the temple like I told everyone. Tomorrow I'll... tomorrow I'll do everything I didn't do today.

I hate resting. It feels like giving up. But even I can't wait forever without closing my eyes. Even stubborn has its limits.

I pull my blanket around me, not because I'm cold, just because it feels like armor. Tomorrow. Promise promise.

Let me check my debts one more time before I sleep, make sure I understand what the household owes. And then... rest.  Looked around. Already checked that. Nobody's here.

Energy at 2910. Money at 4355. Household owes 360 upkeep + 120 head tax = 480 today. We can cover it. But I don't know if Papa and Mama are pooling their earnings or if...

Actually, I should stop. I'm tired-wired, the kind where my brain won't stop gnawing at the same bones.

Rest. I need to rest.

But first—one more check. On me. On what I believe about today. I need to consolidate what I know before I let it all go fuzzy in sleep.

Let me check my goals and beliefs one more time, then I'm done. I'm calling it.  Just checking my debts first, making sure I understand the household situation. Then I'll rest.

output:
*Halcyon sits at home, alone, the quiet pressing against her like a weight. She's been running all day—mill to cafe to street to home again—and now, finally stillness. But the stillness doesn't feel like rest. It feels like something she forgot to do.*

*She thinks about Mama, about the conversation at the mill that cut off mid-sentence. About Camille, who was supposed to be safe at the temple but ended up following her to the street instead. About Yara's words, still echoing: "I was chasing shadows where there were none."*

*She's tired. Eleven years old, and already tired of being the one who notices things, who keeps promises, who tries to hold everyone together when nobody asked her to.*

*But there's Papa. Milo. Somewhere in this town, probably still at work. She hasn't seen him since—when? This morning? The day is blurring.*

"I should check on Papa," she murmurs to herself, though there's no one to hear. "Make sure he knows... make sure he knows we're all still here."

*She stands up, still holding tight to the instinct that someone needs her to be brave. Even if she's not sure what brave looks like right now.*

*But first—she needs to remember. Where has everyone been today? Where is Papa working now? The memory feels scattered, and she doesn't want to chase more shadows.*

*She closes her eyes, breathing slow, trying to piece together where her family has been, what faces she's seen, what words were spoken and what were only thought.*  *Halcyon's fingers trace the edge of the table, remembering.*

*Mama was at the mill, last she saw. Grinding wheat, probably still there. The conversation cut off, but Mama was working—she's a barista, but she goes wherever there's work to do. Always has. That's not new.*

*Papa... Papa's a day laborer. He goes where there's labor needed. She hasn't seen him today, not really. Not since morning maybe. The town's big and he's small in it, moving between sites, doing what needs doing.*

*She thinks about Camille, her sister, eight years old and learning already how to be useful. Saw her at the street, with Esme and Ezra. Learning the trade, Yara said. That's good—that's what matters.*

*But it's late now. Almost night. And the family is scattered like seeds in wind.*

"I should find Papa," she whispers. "Make sure he knows... knows we're all accounted for. That's what I do. That's what I've always done."

*But she's tired. And home is warm, and safe, and empty.*

*She could go out. Look for him. But where? The street? The sites? He's a day laborer—he could be anywhere work needs hands.*

*Or she could wait. Wait for them all to come home, the way families are supposed to do.*

*She's good at waiting. She's waited her whole life for one thing or another.*

"But that's not fair," she murmurs, the phrase slipping out automatic, half a joke to herself. "Waiting's not the same as... as doing something."

*She stands, then sits again. Uncertain. Eleven years old and already carrying the weight of keeping track of everyone.*

*In the end, she decides on something simple. Something she's been meaning to do all day but kept putting off, kept chasing from place to place.*

*She needs to eat. She's been running since dawn, and she's empty inside. Not just tired—hungry. And there's no food here, at home. Nothing in her hands.*

*She could go out. Find something. But the prices she saw... bread at 30 sim, 45 sim. She has sim—4355 of it—but paying that much for bread feels wrong. Like giving up.*

*She remembers her own family's trade. Remembers what she's already good at, what Papa taught her before she even knew she was learning.*

"There must be timber," she says softly. "There's always timber. And timber becomes planks, and planks become... something. Something useful."

*She stands, decision made. Not chasing shadows this time. Just doing what she knows how to do, what she's always been good at.*

"Promise promise," she whispers to the empty room. "I'll be useful. I'll do what I can."

*She moves toward the door, toward the night, toward whatever work is still waiting in this town that never quite stops moving.* *She's walking now, out into the cooling evening. Five ticks to the forest. Time to think, time to breathe, time to be alone with the quiet that doesn't feel so heavy when you're moving through it.*

*She won't fell timber in the dark. She knows that. But she can be there when the light comes. Can be ready. Can do something useful while the rest of the world sleeps.*

*That's enough, she tells herself. That's brave enough for tonight.*

output:
"That's not fair!" The day's barely started and I'm already lost—well, not lost exactly, but somewhere I didn't mean to be. Kasukabe Forest, and my dawn walk was supposed to be through the *park*, not all the way out here.

I rub my eyes. Mama's probably worried sick, or worse, she's not even home to notice. Papa was selling timber at the college yesterday, but—wait. The college. That's where I should be too. School. I missed school. That's... that's not good. That's not good at all.

Mireille Jarrah's here with me, looking just as confused probably. I don't know her well—she builds things, I think. She's older. I'm only eleven, I shouldn't be wandering forests at dawn with strangers.

*Think, Halcyon, think.* I keep making promises I can't keep. "I'll stay with Camille." "I'll find Mama." "I'll be good." And then I wander off again. That's not bravery, that's just... that's just getting lost with extra steps.

I want to go home. No—that's not right either. I want to do it *right* this time. Find someone. Explain properly. Not just leave notes in the air that nobody hears.

But first, I need to know where everyone actually *is*. Not where I think they are—where the town says they are. Because I keep guessing wrong, and guessing wrong means standing alone while the sun comes up over the wrong trees.

I'll ask. Properly. Find someone who knows something. She builds things, like I thought. Forestry too—so she's not lost here, she probably came here on purpose. That makes one of us.

The thing is... I don't want to bother her. She's working, probably, and I'm just a kid who walked too far. But I'm also scared, if I'm honest, and I'm never supposed to admit that, especially not to myself, but the forest is big and the paths all look the same and I was supposed to be at school and—

I need to go back. But I should say something first. Be polite. Not just run away anymore. That's what keeps making this worse.

"Mireille," I'd say, if I was braver than I feel. "I walked too far. I'm trying to get to school. Or home. Either one, promise promise, so my family knows I'm not lost."

But she might not even care. She's older. She has her own work.

I'll just... I'll just start walking back. To town. To anywhere with people I know. The government's maybe open? Or the school—if I'm late, at least I should *be* there, not wandering in trees.

I'll go to the college. Where Papa was. Where I'm supposed to be. It's daytime now, people will be there, and maybe I can still learn something, maybe I can still make this day mean something more than just wandering.  Good. Walking. Nine ticks to get there, that's... that's a while. But I'll be moving, and moving is better than standing still feeling small.

I'll wait it out. Rest while I walk, if that's how it works. Keep my energy for when I actually need it. Not waste it on talking to myself, even though that's what I'm doing right now, inside my head where nobody can hear.

That's the whole problem, isn't it? I keep thinking things, but thinking isn't the same as saying, and saying isn't the same as being heard. I need to be heard today. I need to find Mama, or Papa, or someone who knows where Camille ended up, because I promised to keep her safe and I haven't even seen her since yesterday and that's not fair to anyone, especially not to her.

So I'll walk. And when I get there, I'll do it right. Find someone. Speak proper words. Not just hopes floating off into nowhere.  Still walking. Still going. Nine ticks felt long in my head but I guess they're just... they're just happening, one after another, and I'm moving through the forest toward the college where I should have been all along.

I hope Papa's still there. Or someone who knows where he went. Or Mama. Anyone, really. I'm tired of being the only Quarshie I can find.

I'll rest again. Keep walking. Get there. That's all I can do now.  Still in the forest. Still walking. Mireille's still here too—maybe she's going the same way, or maybe she's just... also here. I don't know. I should probably say something, but I'm shy around strangers until they prove they're friendly, and she hasn't said anything to me either.

So we just... walk together. Separate but together. Like how I've been with my own family lately.

I'll keep going. College soon. Promise promise. I need to stop just resting and actually get somewhere. The system is telling me I'm stuck in a loop—resting over and over without actually arriving. I've been walking to Oak Hill College for what feels like forever, but just pausing doesn't make the walk finish.

I should let the walk complete. Stop pausing and actually arrive.
